opportunities.title: APEX Awards

amount.raw: Applicants can apply for up to £200,000. Research costs must represent no more than 25% of the total award value excluding public engagement costs; public engagement costs up to £10,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record and proven ability to lead collaborative work; hold a permanent or fixed-term position covering the duration of the award; have teaching and admin duties from which they can be relieved; based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Lead applicants may include up to two Co-applicants covering a different Academy remit.
opportunities.summary: APEX Awards (Academies Partnership in Supporting Excellence in Cross-disciplinary research), in partnership with the Royal Society and Royal Academy of Engineering and supported by the Leverhulme Trust, support established independent researchers to pursue interdisciplinary, curiosity-driven research spanning science, engineering, and the social sciences and humanities. Awards can be held for up to 24 months.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; no prior British Academy funding required; some prior public engagement experience expected. Previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: SHAPE Involve and Engage supports ambitious public engagement projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a gallery, archive, library or museum (GLAM organisation) or a performing arts organisation. Projects run between 1 April 2027 and 31 December 2028.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027

amount.raw: The symposium covers travel, accommodation, and visa costs. Seed funding will be made available for which participants can apply for international collaborations.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany, in the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Invites early career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', held 21-23 April 2027, bringing together around fifteen early career researchers from the UK and fifteen from Germany to encourage collaboration and networking.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: Covered under FEC regime; Academy funds 80 per cent of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC. Fellowship tenable for three years.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences based at an eligible UK university or recognised research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals eligible regardless of where doctorate obtained; anyone with a UK doctorate; or strong prior association with UK. Viva Voce completed between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. Must not have been appointed to a permanent academic post.
opportunities.summary: Three-year award for an annual cohort of outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards completion of a significant piece of publishable research, strengthening their research and teaching experience and boosting prospects of a permanent academic post. Funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27

amount.raw: The maximum grant is £10,000. Awards are for engagement activities, not time buy-out; not offered on FEC basis.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences, ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based HEI or IRO that will continue for the full duration of the award. Independent researchers without institutional affiliation are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Talent Development Awards promote the acquisition and advancement of skills in relevant areas by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination. Covers core areas like quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities and languages. Awards held for a minimum of six months and up to a maximum of 12 months.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: Up to £300,000 over 2 years, offered at 80% FEC (total project value at 100% FEC may not exceed £375,000).

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute with an established role lasting at least the duration of the award, of postdoctoral or above status, spending at least 20% of their time on the award. Involvement of overseas Co-Applicants is required; collaboration across disciplines required.
opportunities.summary: Supports international interdisciplinary research projects led by UK-based researchers in the humanities and social sciences working with international partners, on the theme of Mobilities (movement of people, things and ideas). Projects run for 24 months, beginning March/April 2027. Supported by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: Up to £150,000 for 12 months in duration (with Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent). Up to two one-year fellowships.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences. Applications invited in areas of Security/Defence/Resilience, Indo-European Relations, Technology and AI, and Strategy-Making in Europe.
opportunities.summary: Global Innovation Fellowships provide UK-based early- and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences the opportunity to embed themselves in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin, developing their skills, networks and careers in the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors. Funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs

amount.raw: Funding of up to £4,000 to support additional needs; in exceptional circumstances bids above £4,000 may be considered.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Available for both current British Academy award-holders and for applicants who intend to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months and need support with submitting their application. Applicant must meet eligibility for the scheme they intend to apply for.
opportunities.summary: Funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require, in addition to the amount already requested for research expenses. Examples include specific equipment to overcome barriers for disabled researchers, assistance for applicants with sensory impairment, caring costs, and support to make an application. Applications reviewed on a case-by-case basis; offered on a rolling deadline.
